title: Determine Whether Matrix Can Be Obtained By Rotation
statement:
`mat` and `target` are square `n x n` grids of `0`s and `1`s. You may turn `mat` by a quarter turn (90 degrees) as many times as you like, including not at all.

Return `true` when some number of quarter turns makes `mat` identical to `target` cell by cell, and `false` otherwise.
notes:
## Intuition

Four quarter turns bring a grid back to where it started, so only four candidates exist: turned 0, 1, 2 or 3 times. A direct method builds each turned copy and compares it to `target`. We can skip the copies: each turn is just a formula for which cell of `mat` lands at position `(i, j)`, so one pass over `target` can test all four turns at once.

## Approach

1. Keep four flags in `fits`, one per number of clockwise quarter turns, all starting `true`.
2. For every cell `(i, j)`, read `value = target[i][j]` and compare it with the cell of `mat` that each turn puts there:
   - 0 turns: `mat[i][j]`
   - 1 turn: `mat[n - 1 - j][i]`
   - 2 turns: `mat[n - 1 - i][n - 1 - j]`
   - 3 turns: `mat[j][n - 1 - i]`
3. A mismatch turns that flag off for good.
4. Return `true` if any flag survived.

## Example 1, step by step

`mat = [[0,1],[1,0]]`, `target = [[1,0],[0,1]]`, `n = 2`. At `(0, 0)`, `value = 1`: `mat[0][0] = 0` clears `fits[0]`, `mat[1][0] = 1` keeps `fits[1]`, `mat[1][1] = 0` clears `fits[2]`, `mat[0][1] = 1` keeps `fits[3]`. The remaining cells agree with both one and three turns, so `fits = [false, true, false, true]` and the answer is `true`.

## Complexity

- Time: O(n²): every cell is visited once, with four comparisons.
- Space: O(1) besides the four flags.

## Pitfalls

- Zero turns counts: identical grids answer `true`.
- A mirror image (transpose or flip) is not a rotation; check the index formulas on a 3 x 3 grid.
- Returning as soon as one cell matches some turn is wrong: a single turn must match every cell.

## Variables

| Name | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `n` | side length of both grids |
| `fits[k]` | whether `k` clockwise quarter turns still match every cell checked so far |
| `i`, `j` | row and column in `target` |
| `value` | `target[i][j]` |

narration.2: Both grids are n by n.
narration.3: One flag per rotation: 0, 1, 2 or 3 clockwise quarter turns, all possible so far.
narration.5: Visit every cell of target once.
narration.7: The value every rotation must produce at this cell.
narration.8: Without turning, mat must match cell for cell.
narration.9: After one clockwise turn, row i, column j comes from mat[n - 1 - j][i].
narration.10: After two turns, the cell comes from the opposite corner position.
narration.11: After three turns (one counter-clockwise), it comes from mat[j][n - 1 - i].
narration.14: Some rotation matched every cell exactly when one flag is still true.
